text:
Oh, absolutely. Because what the world was desperately crying out for was a pair of trousers that you can’t see, can’t feel, and definitely can’t wear to a job interview without looking like you’re having a very public, very naked breakdown. The fashion industry, in its infinite wisdom, has finally solved the problem of "too much fabric" by removing the fabric entirely. It’s brilliant, really. You get the slimming effect of a vacuum seal without the inconvenience of actually being clothed, and your wallet stays light because you’re essentially buying air. It’s the ultimate minimalist statement: "I have nothing to hide, and nothing to wear."

But since you asked, and because even invisible jeans need a source of inspiration, pearls are typically found in **oysters** (and other mollusks like clams and mussels). They are formed when an irritant gets inside the shell, and the mollusk coats it in nacre to protect itself. So, in a way, pearls are just oyster jewelry made of regret and calcium. Much like these invisible jeans, they are a response to an irritation, but at least the oyster gets to keep its shell.
